loom_consolidation.operator_requirement: Studio spec forbids a second blob tier; your job is to consolidate, not to comply retroactively.
loom_consolidation.source: Operator mission attachment; explicit permission to create extra MTs preserving added scope.
loom_consolidation.scope: Convert live Loom original and derivative writers/readers to ArtifactStore, preserving asset identities, references, routes, Range and recoverable migration. This is implementation scope, not a deferred separate WP.

patterns: Database transactions protect catalog/event/idempotency records, not filesystem writes.
Digest, length and MIME bind content identity; completed transfer alone is not verification.
Preserve HTTP Range semantics; whole-object hash requires whole-object verification before a slice is served.
research_basis.selected_approach: Reuse canonical ArtifactStore materialization and verification, then transactionally bind the existing Loom asset identity with expected-state protection and event/idempotency evidence. Canonically reread binding and bytes before any legacy retirement. Preserve all original/derivative references and routes.
reuse: ArtifactStore streaming write, manifests and verified reads
stage_artifacts request-hash idempotency and catalog/event transaction pattern
Loom tier selection and Range HTTP tests
rejected: Deleting originals before independent destination proof
Assuming database rollback undoes filesystem writes
risks: Crash leaves incomplete destination or orphan
Full-object verified Range reads incur buffering cost
mitigations: Resumable idempotent migration; retain old bytes until canonical proof
Typed fail-closed errors; preserve damaged source for diagnosis
Use governed schema/pin surface; no implicit reset or unproven upgrade claim
Preserve existing behavior and document measured resource limits
research_basis.validation: Real embedded database and on-disk ArtifactStore; crash/retry boundaries, original and derivative identity/reference preservation, concurrent publication, full and Range HTTP bytes/headers, corruption outside requested range. No skipped embedded setup may count as pass.
